page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.4xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance hosted on a KVM hypervisor. The system allocates 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at 2.6 GHz, utilizing simultaneous multithreading. It features 32 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 core-to-memory distribution of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache structure includes 32 KB L1 data, 0.5 MB L2, and 16 MB L3 cache. The CPU instruction set includes AVX, AES-NI, and SHA-NI, but excludes AVX-512 extensions. The instance comes with no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached disks, and provides a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier multi-threaded capacity alongside distinct single-thread and memory throughput constraints. Multi-core performance aligns with industry midpoints, registering a Geekbench multi-core score of 7305 and a PassMark CPU score of 18931.51. Software compilation with Clang and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression perform solidly within middle-tier expectations. However, single-core processing demonstrates lower relative output, evidenced by a bottom-decile stress-ng single-core score of 765.19. Additionally, while cached memory bandwidth reaches 800.3 GB/sec, uncached 256 MB memory transfers decrease to 29.73 GB/sec for reads and 15.34 GB/sec for writes, placing uncached memory operations in the bottom 25th percentile.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the absence of onboard NVMe drives and GPU accelerators creates a straightforward compute profile focused on raw multi-core scaling. The architecture is best suited for horizontally scaled web services, continuous integration build jobs, Redis caching layers, and general backend processing where workloads leverage multiple threads and interact with remote storage.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at 2.6 GHz on a KVM hypervisor. Built on x86_64 architecture, it delivers 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores, 32 GB of RAM (2 GB per vCPU), and a 16 MB L3 cache. The instance contains no bundled local storage and includes a 5 Gbps baseline network capability. Performance benchmarks show balanced multi-core compute capability, achieving 7305 in Geekbench multi-core and 18931.51 in PassMark CPU tests, accompanied by average throughput in static web serving and software compilation. Conversely, uncached memory bandwidth and single-core stress testing indicate bottom-quartile throughput. Given its 1:2 compute-to-memory profile and lack of integrated storage, the instance fits multi-threaded web application hosting, build systems, and distributed microservices using detached cloud disks.
